note: Singapore's three largest banks are DBS (with POSB), OCBC and UOB. UOB's card fee pages answer 404 to this research (2026-10-30) and its cards page links no fee schedule, so DBS and OCBC are written. DBS's annual fee page (read 2026-10-30; fees include GST): most of its cards cost 196.20 dollars a year for the principal card, the first year waived for a new principal cardholder (written; this file left it out until now), the Woman's MasterCard 163.50, the Vantage Card 599.50 with no first-year waiver, the Live Fresh Student Card 196.20 waived for five years. A spending waiver for the next year is written where the page states one and doesn't say it ceased on 1 August 2026: the Takashimaya American Express (25,000 dollars a year) and the Woman's MasterCard (15,000); the Woman's World MasterCard's, Altitude cards' and Vantage's ceased that day and aren't written. The Treasures Black Elite (closed to new applicants), the MasterCard Platinum (for former ANZ customers only), the SAFRA card (free while a SAFRA member) and the Chromo card (not on the fee page) aren't written. DBS's card rates and fees page (read 2026-10-30, rendered in a browser, the table loading by script): finance charges 27.8% a year; a cash advance 8% of the amount, at least 15 dollars, and 28.5% a year; 3% a year more after a missed minimum payment, written as a penalty rate of 30.8%; the minimum payment 3% of the statement balance or 50 dollars, whichever is greater, plus anything overdue or over the limit; a late payment 100 dollars; spending in another currency 3.25% in all (the network's 1% and the bank's fee). No grace period or over-limit fee is stated. OCBC's credit card page (read 2026-10-30): each card's principal annual fee, the first two years free (the 90°N Card's annual service fee of 54 dollars, its first year free), and the spending that waives it automatically (10,000 dollars a year; 5,000 on the BEST-OCBC card); the Premier Visa Infinite free (for OCBC Premier customers); interest 26.88% a year and a 100-dollar late charge. Its INFINITY Cashback and VOYAGE cards show no fee on the page and aren't written. OCBC's fees and charges for credit cards (dated July 2024, read 2026-10-30) gives 27.78% a year, above the card page's later 26.88%, which is written; after a missed minimum payment 30.78% a year (written as the penalty rate); a cash advance 8% or 15 dollars, whichever is greater, and 28.92% a year; the minimum payment 3% of the total balance or 50 dollars, whichever is higher, plus anything overdue; 23 days free of interest from the statement date when no balance is carried, written as the grace period; over the limit 50 dollars; spending in another currency 1% plus 2.25%, written as 3.25%. The 1% fee on Singapore-dollar spending processed abroad isn't written.
